decisions.reason: The board remains a four-layer design, and that layer count is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message Event; changing the outline to 70×50 does not alter it.
The 70×50 resize applies to the legacy main board, not the power board, so the power-board form-factor and mounting requirements remain unchanged.
Resizing and rearranging the main board does not necessarily change the required top-edge placement, relative connector alignment, or straight interboard cable routing.
The client rejects connector consolidation and preserves the existing individual JST-based interface; no connector type, pinout, partition, or power-chain attribute necessarily changes.
The main-board outline change does not alter the four-board architecture or the inventory of separate functional boards.
The client's acceptance of ESP32 edge placement is already represented by the candidate's same-message Event, and the 70×50 outline does not establish any additional antenna-placement change.
The source concerns the legacy main-board outline and its individual connectors, not the power board's battery connector placement, orientation, or accessibility.
The legacy main-board resize does not change the LED daughterboard's size description, LED count, or selected LED component.
No charge-status display, external charge-LED connector, resistor, or population requirement is changed by the main-board outline decision.
The board dimensions do not alter the DCDC1 programmed voltage, current rating, compensation purpose, or 3.3V system-rail behavior.
The source does not change I2C cable length, bus speed, pull-ups, series resistors, or signal-conditioning topology.
Keeping individual JST connectors and resizing the main board does not change the defined panel-control connector inventory, signal assignments, or on-board button policy.
